camera.setups: Virtual three.js camera: mostly a static medium full-body shot of the host at chest height; slow orbits of a few degrees, quick push-ins to the face, one pull-back to a wide; examples framed with the host small lower-left and the subject big right.
camera.gear_guess: three.js in one HTML file, WebGLRenderer at 270 x 480, CSS/nearest upscale

lighting.lighting_overall: One warm directional sun from the upper left plus a cool hemisphere fill; flat-shaded faces so every facet is one tone; no shadows except a dark blob under the feet.

grade.grade_overall: Bright, saturated, slightly warm; evening sky gradient violet-blue to pink; dithered.

editing.editing: One-word captions on every word, hard cuts on the beat, a white flash once, a shrink-to-card and back once, a split-screen before/after once; the host never leaves the screen until the examples.

format.format: Talking low-poly mascot explains a numbered list of rules, demonstrating each on itself, then shows example cutaways and a CTA board.

style.render_style: Real-time low-poly 3D (three.js) rendered at 270 x 480 and upscaled 4x with nearest-neighbour: PS1-style chunky pixels with crisp UI on top.
style.outline: None. Shapes separate by flat facet tones and texture; the slice reveals a cut face with bright orange triangle edges.
style.shading: Flat shading, one tone per triangle, sun from the upper left; ordered dither on gradients; no specular, no soft shadows; a dark blob shadow under feet.
style.shape_language: Faceted, blocky, about 300 triangles per character: box torso, box limbs, faceted ball head with cone ears, chunky boxy shoes; subjects simplified to big readable volumes.
style.texture: Tiny 64 px textures painted by code and sampled nearest: fabric speckle on the suit, stripes on fur, tufted grass, plank grain on the fence, a painted face; visible texels.
style.type_ui: Header top-left: a yellow numeral 'k/N' plus a short rule in white rounded heavy type with a dark outline (about 60 px at 1080 wide), the key word in yellow; one-word captions centre-low in heavy white with a thick dark outline (about 80 px); in-world labels yellow with dark outline and a thin orange leader line.
style.motion_style: Snappy: poses switch on each sentence, small idle bob, short camera pushes and orbits; vertices jitter slightly (snapped to the pixel grid).
style.signature: The subject sliced open down the middle, halves sliding apart, a dark violet cut face with orange triangle edges, and one yellow label with a leader line naming the part inside.
style.do_not_copy: The 'made with visualizemy.com' watermark, the raccoon, the yellow suit with red tie, the backyard set as-is, the topic (making low-poly videos with an AI), the rule texts, the 'link in bio' CTA wording and the example subjects (volcano, heart, coffee machine).

story.summary: A low-poly mascot teaches a six-step recipe for its own look, demonstrating each step on its own body, then shows the recipe applied to other subjects; charm comes from the mascot reacting to what is being done to it.
story.hook: 0-6 s: the finished look on screen at once, a sign board fills with six numbered steps while the host promises it is short and knocks down the expected objection.
highlights: 6.5-11 s: the bad default first (a smooth glossy toy version, the host says 'Ew'), so every rule after it reads as a fix
11.5-35 s: each rule gets a numbered header 'k/6' at the top and is demonstrated on the host immediately (shards, textures, tiny render, before/after, slice, poses), one visible change per rule
25-29 s: the slice reveals the inside with a single label and a deadpan joke: the cutaway is the signature image
35-39 s: three quick cutaway examples on plain coloured backdrops prove the method transfers
